inputs.label: Onsoo Botanicals US market entry briefing pack

storyline.governing_thought: Enter the US via Amazon in 2027, staged behind an ad-cost gate: the only US route within the board's limits, it pays back only below 28.6% ACoS

exec_summary.text: The US is worth entering, and Amazon is the way in: K-beauty is gaining share and Onsoo's test is growing fast

sub_points.text: Amazon has 41% of US K-beauty skincare sales; 61% of buyers shop there most
Pilot sales grew 89% in six months, but repeat is 29%, against 48% in Korea

exec_summary.text: The retail-led route breaks all three board limits and rests on sell-through Onsoo has not earned

sub_points.text: Its cash need passes the $18M cap in 2029 and reaches $20.8M by 2030
Group margin would fall to 4.5% in 2027, below the 8% floor

exec_summary.text: Amazon-led fits the limits, but only just, and reaches $26.4M rather than $40M by 2030

sub_points.text: Payback by 2030 needs ACoS below 28.6% on average; the pilot ran at 28%
Japan returns more cash above 25.9% ACoS but builds only a $7M business

exec_summary.text: Launch in stages: commit to 2027, decide 2028 on ad cost and the tariff, add retail only above 20% awareness

sub_points.text: Four gates: ACoS, US labels, repeat at 31%, and 20% awareness for retail
National retail in 2029 would leave the US $11.9M short of payback in 2030

next_steps.action: Approve Amazon-led entry for 2027 with a cash envelope sized to the worst-case need, not the $18M cap
Set up the US entity, MoCRA registration and US-compliant labels; take the listings over from the cross-border seller
Run a monthly ACoS, repeat-rate and awareness dashboard, and re-run the payback model after the tariff ruling
Hold the 2028 go / no-go review on gate 1, with the Japan scale-up plan ready as the fallback
Cost a smaller regional retail test as an alternative to the 600-door national launch

constraints.item: Investment cap: peak negative cumulative US cash of no more than $18M through 2030
constraints.effect: Option B passes it in 2029 and reaches $20.8M; Option A peaks at $1.9M ($3.9M at 32% ACoS and 25% duty)

constraints.item: Payback: cumulative US cash back to zero by end-2030
constraints.effect: Option A meets it only below 28.6% average ACoS (26.9% with a 25% duty); the governing thought and exec item 3 say so

constraints.item: Group operating margin at or above 8% in every year
constraints.effect: Option B breaks it in 2027-29 (4.5% in 2027); a 2029 retail layer on Option A breaks it in 2029 (about 6.3%)

constraints.item: Bandwidth for only one major launch in 2027
constraints.effect: the options are mutually exclusive; Japan stays the fallback for 2028 if gate 1 fails
no route reaches it; Option A reaches $26.4M; the exec summary says so rather than claiming the ambition

constraints.item: Possible duty rise from 15% to 25% (decision mid-2027, after the board meeting)
constraints.effect: lowers the payback threshold to 26.9% and, at the pilot's 28% ACoS, pushes end-2030 cash to about -$0.7M; the plan reviews it before the 2028 budget

constraints.item: Advertising cost at scale (agency median 32% for $5M-20M brands) against the planned 25%
constraints.effect: at 32% Option A ends 2030 $2.3M short of payback; this is the gate

constraints.item: Korean-only labels (6% of pilot reviews) and MoCRA labeling compliance
constraints.effect: gate 2; covered by the $0.8M setup budget
not modelled; a stronger won would lower Option A's margin of safety (about -$1.2M at end-2030 for a 10% stronger won, red-team estimate); noted in the slide 12 assumptions

alternatives.option: Option J: Japan scale-up instead of the US in 2027
alternatives.why: meets every limit and returns more cash by 2030 whenever US ACoS averages above about 25.9%, but leaves a $7M business in a market growing 1.5% a year against $26.4M in a segment growing 16%; kept as the fallback if gate 1 fails

alternatives.option: Option B: national retail launch in 600 doors in 2027 (board member's view)
alternatives.why: breaks the cap, payback and margin floor even on its own inputs; on the evidence (2.6 units a door, no halo) it loses $26.4M by 2030

alternatives.option: Staged Amazon entry: commit to 2027 only, with an end-2027 go / no-go on ACoS and the tariff
alternatives.why: keeps exposure to the 2027 launch while the two most uncertain inputs are tested; adopted as the launch plan

alternatives.option: CEO's hypothesis: add specialty retail from 2029 once Amazon passes $10M and awareness 15%
alternatives.why: at 15% awareness median sell-through (3.5) is below the 4.0 removal line, and a 2029 national layer leaves the US $11.9M short of payback in 2030 and breaks the margin floor; gate moved to 20% and decided separately

failure_threshold.threshold: above about 28.6% (26.9% if the duty rises to 25%) Option A no longer pays back by end-2030; above about 25.9% Japan returns more cash by 2030
failure_threshold.range: Option A cumulative cash at end-2030: low -$3.4M (32% ACoS, 25% duty) / mid +$0.4M (28% pilot ACoS) / high +$2.4M (planned 25%)

consistency.headline: Enter the US via Amazon in 2027, staged behind an ad-cost gate: the only US route within the board's limits, it pays back only below 28.6% ACoS
consistency.fix: Red-team review: changed 'the only route' to 'the only US route' (Japan also meets the limits), added the payback condition to the governing thought, stated that $40M is not reached, and staged the launch behind an end-2027 gate
